doc:
For many type classes, we have a definition that lets us transfer instances from one type to another
using an equivalence, such as `Equiv.mul` for `Mul`.
Constructing data instances in this way is discouraged because the resulting data is inefficient
to unfold. To somewhat mitigate this problem, in these definitions we don't write the
projections on `Equiv` in the usual way using `Equiv.symm` and `DFunLike.coe`, and instead use
`Equiv.toFun` and `Equiv.invFun` directly. As a result, unification has to do less unfolding.

Note also that when constructing data instances in this way, it usually helps to use
`fast_instance%` to get a faster instance.

doc:
Let `A', A, B', B` be subgroups of `G`.
If `A' = B'` and `A = B`, then the quotients `A / (A' ⊓ A)` and `B / (B' ⊓ B)` are isomorphic.

Applying this equiv is nicer than rewriting along the equalities, since the type of
`(A'.subgroupOf A : Subgroup A)` depends on `A`.

value.text:
fun {G} [Group G] {A' A B' B} [(A'.subgroupOf A).Normal] [(B'.subgroupOf B).Normal] h' h =>
  (QuotientGroup.quotientMapSubgroupOfOfLe ⋯ ⋯).toMulEquiv
    (QuotientGroup.quotientMapSubgroupOfOfLe ⋯ ⋯) ⋯ ⋯

theorem QuotientAddGroup.strictMono_comap_prod_map.{u} {G : Type u} [AddGroup G] (N : AddSubgroup G)
  [nN : N.Normal] :
  StrictMono fun H => (AddSubgroup.comap N.subtype H, AddSubgroup.map (QuotientAddGroup.mk' N) H)

theorem QuotientAddGroup.map_normal.{u} {G : Type u} [AddGroup G] (N : AddSubgroup G) [nN : N.Normal]
  (M : AddSubgroup G) [nM : M.Normal] : (AddSubgroup.map (QuotientAddGroup.mk' N) M).Normal

theorem QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientAux_mk_mk.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G)
  [nN : N.Normal] (M : Subgroup G) [nM : M.Normal] (h : N ≤ M) (x : G) :
  (QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientAux N M h) ↑↑x = ↑x

theorem QuotientGroup.comap_map_mk'.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G] (N H : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] :
  Subgroup.comap (QuotientGroup.mk' N) (Subgroup.map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) H) = N ⊔ H

theorem QuotientGroup.comap_comap_center.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G] {H₁ : Subgroup G} [H₁.Normal]
  {H₂ : Subgroup (G ⧸ H₁)} [H₂.Normal] :
  Subgroup.comap (QuotientGroup.mk' H₁)
      (Subgroup.comap (QuotientGroup.mk' H₂) (Subgroup.center ((G ⧸ H₁) ⧸ H₂))) =
    Subgroup.comap (QuotientGroup.mk' (Subgroup.comap (QuotientGroup.mk' H₁) H₂))
      (Subgroup.center (G ⧸ Subgroup.comap (QuotientGroup.mk' H₁) H₂))

theorem QuotientAddGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientAux_mk.{u} {G : Type u} [AddGroup G]
  (N : AddSubgroup G) [nN : N.Normal] (M : AddSubgroup G) [nM : M.Normal] (h : N ≤ M) (x : G ⧸ N) :
  (QuotientAddGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientAux N M h) ↑x =
    (QuotientAddGroup.map N M (AddMonoidHom.id G) h) x

theorem QuotientAddGroup.kerLift_mk.{u, v} {G : Type u} [AddGroup G] {H : Type v} [AddGroup H] (φ : G →+ H)
  (g : G) : (QuotientAddGroup.kerLift φ) ↑g = φ g

theorem QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom_comp.{u} {A B : Type u} [CommGroup A] [CommGroup B] (f : A →* B)
  (g : B →* A) (n : ℤ) :
  QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom (f.comp g) n =
    (QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom f n).comp (QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom g n)

doc: **Noether's third isomorphism theorem** for groups: `(G / N) / (M / N) ≃* G / M`.

value.text:
fun {G} [Group G] N [N.Normal] M [M.Normal] h =>
  (QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientAux N M h).toMulEquiv
    (QuotientGroup.map M (Subgroup.map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) M) (QuotientGroup.mk' N) ⋯) ⋯ ⋯

theorem QuotientAddGroup.prodEquiv_apply.{u, v} {G : Type u} [AddGroup G] {H : Type v} [AddGroup H]
  (A : AddSubgroup G) (B : AddSubgroup H) (q : (G × H) ⧸ A.prod B) :
  (QuotientAddGroup.prodEquiv A B) q =
    Quotient.liftOn' q
      (fun x =>
        match x with
        | (g, h) => (↑g, ↑h))
      ⋯

theorem QuotientGroup.prodMulEquiv_apply.{u, v} {G : Type u} [Group G] {H : Type v} [Group H]
  (A : Subgroup G) (B : Subgroup H) [A.Normal] [B.Normal] (q : (G × H) ⧸ A.prod B) :
  (QuotientGroup.prodMulEquiv A B) q = Quotient.liftOn' q (fun x => (↑x.1, ↑x.2)) ⋯
